newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots up.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots up.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly down on Wednesday with falls on the domestic A share markets today reducing fund demand on the repurchase market, traders said.
The annual rate for the most active seven-day contract fell to 8.45 percent from 11.80 percent on Tuesday.
Total turnover of the six-contract market fell sharply to 3.8 million lots from 6.8 million lots.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
Traders said the fall on the A share markets was the main reason behind today's sharp losses on the repo market.
"The plunge on the A share markets made fund demand sharply down on the repo market," said one trader. "The rates are unlikely to rebound on Thursday due to uncertainties on the A share markets."
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly up on Wednesday boosted by good sales of the latest batch of state debt being issued from May 1 to May 31, traders said.
The most actively traded 10-year bond that matures in June 2006 rose to 120.55 yuan from 119.85 yuan.
Combined volume of the seven-contract market fell to 605,528 lots from 883,272 lots.
"Good sales of the latest three-year treasury notes have made investors believe the spot market will recover to some extent in the short term," one trader said.
The spot market has been weak in the past few months with the active stock markets sucking money out of the spot contracts.
Traders said they expeced the spot contracts to rise slightly in the next few days.
